title: Move around the 3D viewport
summary: Orbit, pan and zoom the view, jump to front and top views, and frame the whole scene.

steps.say: Make sure the Layout tab is selected in the top bar. Click Layout if another tab is highlighted.

checks.prompt: Is the Layout workspace tab highlighted in the top bar, with a large 3D view in the middle of the window?

hints: Layout is the first tab to the right of the Help menu, at the very top.
If you see no tabs, open File, New, General to start a fresh scene.
steps.why: The lessons point at places on screen that match the Layout workspace.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, hold the middle mouse button and drag to orbit around the scene.

check.prompt: Has the viewing angle of the 3D viewport changed compared to the start, so the cube is seen from a different side?

hints: The middle button is the scroll wheel. Press it down like a button and move the mouse.
No middle button? Drag the colored axis ball in the top right corner of the viewport instead.
steps.why: Orbiting lets you look at your model from every side.

steps.say: Now hold Shift, then hold the middle mouse button and drag. The view slides sideways without turning.

check.prompt: Has the scene shifted sideways or up and down in the 3D viewport without the viewing angle changing?

hints: Keep Shift held down the whole time you drag.
You can also drag the hand icon below the axis ball in the top right of the viewport.
steps.why: Panning moves your view without losing the angle you picked.

steps.say: Roll the mouse wheel to zoom in and out.

check.prompt: Do the objects in the 3D viewport appear noticeably larger or smaller than at the start of this step?

hints: Keep the pointer over the big middle area while you scroll.
Without a wheel, drag the magnifier icon below the axis ball, or press the plus and minus keys on the numpad.
steps.why: Zooming brings details close or shows the whole scene.

steps.say: With your mouse over the 3D viewport, press Numpad 1 for the front view.

checks.prompt: Does the top left of the 3D viewport now show the word Front, with the scene seen straight from the front?

hints: Use the 1 on the numeric keypad, not the 1 above the letters.
Or click the green Y circle with a minus sign on the axis ball, or open View, Viewpoint, Front.
steps.why: Straight views make it easier to line things up.

steps.say: Press Numpad 7 to look down from the top.

checks.prompt: Does the top left of the 3D viewport now show the word Top, with the scene seen from directly above?

hints: The 7 key is the top left key of the numeric keypad.
Or click the blue Z circle on the axis ball, or open View, Viewpoint, Top.
steps.why: The top view works like a floor plan of your scene.

steps.say: Press Home to fit everything in the scene into the view.

checks.prompt: Are the cube, the camera and the light all visible inside the 3D viewport now?

hints: Home is in the small key block above the arrow keys.
Or open the View menu in the viewport header and choose Frame All.
steps.why: Frame All is the quickest way back when you get lost in 3D space.
